DevOps Bootcamp Capstone

Team 2 — "It Works on Our Machines"

An end-to-end automated deployment pipeline: from an idea typed on a board, through GitHub and Jenkins, to a live website running on AWS.

The Team & Responsibilities

Six people, one pipeline. Each owned a piece of the stack.

Edgars

@paradisecreate

Team lead & repository owner. Coordinated the branches and merges.

Minnu

@minnubj

Terraform — Infrastructure as Code. Provisioned the AWS EC2 instance.

Nikunj

 

Docker & containerization. Packaged the website into an image.

Katrina

CI/CD owner

Jenkins pipeline — build, push to ECR, deploy to EC2 & S3, smoke test.

Anton

 

Ansible — server configuration and package setup.

Zlata

@HamsterInItsBall

AWS networking & access — security groups, IAM, connectivity.

Solution Architecture

flowchart LR
    Dev["Developer / Board"] -->|git push| GH["GitHub Repo"]
    GH -->|Poll SCM| J["Jenkins Pipeline"]
    J --> B["Build Docker Image"]
    B --> ECR[("Amazon ECR")]
    ECR --> D["Deploy Container
EC2 : port 80"]
    J --> S3[("Amazon S3
static site")]
    D --> Smoke["Smoke Test
HTTP 200"]

    subgraph Provisioning["One-time provisioning"]
      TF["Terraform (IaC)"] --> EC2[("AWS EC2")]
      ANS["Ansible (config)"] --> EC2
    end

Terraform builds the server · Ansible configures it · Jenkins builds a Docker image · stores it in ECR · deploys to EC2 and S3 · then a smoke test proves the site is up.
